newsitem.title: USA: Tampa, Fla., stadium bond lawsuit gets fast track.
newsitem.headline: Tampa, Fla., stadium bond lawsuit gets fast track.

text.p: Florida's 2nd District Court of Appeal has granted fast-track status to litigation over bond financing for the new Tampa Bay Buccaneers football stadium in Tampa, court officials said.

The ruling, returned Tuesday, gives both sides just two weeks instead of several months to file written briefs. The court did not indicate when it would rule, but officials at the Tampa Sports Authority have said they would not sell revenue bonds for the $168 million stadium until the litigation is resolved.
Hillsborough County residents voted on Sept 3 to raise sales taxes by a half-cent to fund school, road and public safety projects and pay debt service on the stadium bonds.
Former Tampa Mayor William Poe sued to block the financing plan, claiming it would unconstitutionally use public money to benefit the private, for-profit football team.
Hillsborough Circuit Judge Sam Pendino dismissed the lawsuit on Oct 4, but Poe appealed to the Second District Court of Appeal.
Hillsborough County sought the expedited schedule, hoping to resolve the litigation in order to increase its chances of winning Super Bowl in 2000.
